title: Mon amie, son sac, cette adresse
summary: Choose possession and pointing words from the noun, its sound and the intended owner.
objectives: Choose possessives from the owner and the possessed noun, including vowel/mute-h forms.
Use body-part articles without banning possessives in emphatic contexts.
Select demonstratives and possession with generic subjects or conversational on.

sources.label: Public A2 index: topic-coverage reference only

sections.title: Identify the owner, then the noun
paragraphs: A possessive determiner comes before a noun: mon sac. First choose the owner series; then choose the form matching the gender and number of what is possessed, not the owner's gender. Son sac can mean his bag or her bag. French normally does not put an article before a possessive.

Before a feminine singular noun beginning with a vowel or mute h, use mon, ton or son instead of ma, ta or sa: mon amie, ton histoire. The noun stays feminine. A consonant-starting intervening adjective restores ma/ta/sa: ma meilleure amie. Aspirated h blocks this sound-linking: ma honte.
points: Masculine singular / feminine singular / plural: mon/ma/mes; ton/ta/tes; son/sa/ses; notre/notre/nos; votre/votre/vos; leur/leur/leurs.

For the body, a reflexive or indirect pronoun often already identifies whose part it is: je me lave les mains, il a mal au dos. Possessives are natural when ownership needs emphasis or a noun phrase independently describes a feature: mes yeux sont sensibles, elle a posé sa main sur la table.

examples.french: Léa cherche **son sac** et Paul cherche **sa veste**.
examples.english: Léa is looking for her bag and Paul is looking for his jacket.
My friend works with my best friend.

examples.note: A possessive is appropriate in this independent description.

mistakes.why: Histoire begins with mute h; son is used without changing the noun's gender.

sections.title: Generic owners and demonstratives
paragraphs: With generic singular tout le monde, chacun or personne, use son/sa/ses for each person's own possession: chacun prend son sac; personne n'oublie ses clés. In a general instruction il faut présenter sa carte refers to the unspecified person who must act.

On can mean people in general or conversational 'we'. Generic on normally uses son/sa/ses; on meaning our identified group naturally uses notre/nos. Context matters: on garde son billet can also mean each member keeps their own ticket, so do not ban singular possessives after conversational on.

Demonstrative determiners point out a noun: ce before a masculine consonant or aspirated h, cet before a masculine vowel or mute h, cette for feminine singular, ces for all plurals. They can mean this or that, these or those; -ci and -là can clarify contrast.
points: Ce sac, cet appartement, cet hôtel, cette adresse, ces dossiers. Cet is not a feminine form.

examples.english: Each person must bring their card.

examples.french: On visite notre nouvel appartement : on apporte **nos affaires**.
examples.english: We are visiting our new apartment: we are bringing our belongings.
examples.note: On refers to our identified group.

examples.french: En général, on garde **ses documents** chez soi.
examples.english: In general, people keep their documents at home.

examples.french: **Cet hôtel** est près de **cette station** ; **ces chambres** sont libres.
examples.english: This hotel is near this station; these rooms are available.
examples.note: Masculine mute h, feminine singular and plural.

mistakes.why: Adresse is feminine; vowel-starting feminine nouns still take cette.

sections.title: Check the word immediately after the possessive
paragraphs: An adjective can create the vowel contact as well as remove it. Before a feminine noun, mon/ton/son is required when the immediately following adjective starts with a vowel or mute h: the noun itself need not start with a vowel. The adjective and noun remain feminine.

Initial y needs a pronunciation check, not just a letter check. In une yaourtière (feminine, yoghurt maker), y has a consonant sound, so use ma yaourtière. In a name with initial vowel y, such as Yvonne, affectionate mon Yvonne is possible. This sound rule does not change the person's gender.
points: Choose the owner and noun agreement first; then inspect the next sound for the feminine singular substitution.

examples.french: **Mon ancienne collègue** a retrouvé **ma vieille écharpe**.
examples.english: My former colleague found my old scarf.
examples.note: Ancienne starts with a vowel; vieille starts with a consonant.

examples.english: Your yoghurt maker is in your huge kitchen.
examples.note: The initial consonant sound in yaourtière contrasts with the vowel in immense.

practice.prompt: Supply son or sa: Paul cherche ___ chemise.
practice.explanation: Chemise is feminine regardless of Paul's gender.

practice.prompt: Supply mon or ma: ___ amie arrive.
Supply ce, cet or cette: ___ arbre est vieux.
practice.explanation: Arbre is masculine and begins with a vowel.

practice.prompt: Use the usual definite article: Je me brosse ___ dents.
Supply son or sa: Lina a oublié ___ passeport.
Supply ton or ta: ___ histoire est amusante.
practice.explanation: Mute h allows the vowel-linking possessive.

practice.prompt: Supply mon or ma: ___ nouvelle adresse est ici.
Use the possessive meaning my for an independent description: ___ yeux sont sensibles.
practice.explanation: A body-part possessive is appropriate here.

practice.prompt: Generic possession, son/sa/ses: Tout le monde prend ___ affaires.
Generic instruction, son/sa/ses: Il faut signer avec ___ nom.
practice.explanation: The unspecified signer supplies their own name.

practice.prompt: On means our household; choose notre or son: On vend ___ appartement commun.
practice.explanation: The clearly identified shared owner is us.

practice.prompt: Supply ce, cet, cette or ces: ___ entrée est accessible.
Generic on, choose notre or sa: Quand on voyage seul, on prépare ___ valise.
Supply son/sa/ses: Personne ne doit oublier ___ billet.
Supply the plural demonstrative: ___ horaires sont nouveaux.
practice.explanation: Ces works for either gender in the plural.

practice.prompt: Supply their as a possessive determiner: Les voisins cherchent ___ clés.
practice.explanation: Plural possessed noun requires leurs, unlike object pronoun leur.

practice.prompt: Choose ma or mon: ___ ancienne responsable m'a conseillé ce livre.
practice.explanation: Ancienne immediately follows the possessive and begins with a vowel, although responsable begins with a consonant.

practice.prompt: Choose sa or son: Elle range ___ yaourtière. Une yaourtière is feminine and its initial y has a consonant sound.
practice.explanation: A written y is not automatically a vowel sound that triggers son.

production_task.prompt: Send instructions to your household about a move. Mention your shared home, each person's own documents and two objects you can point to.
production_task.model_answer: On prépare notre déménagement samedi. Chacun garde ses documents dans son sac. Cette boîte est pour la cuisine et ces cartons sont pour nos livres. Mon amie vient nous aider.
production_task.translation: We are preparing our move on Saturday. Each person keeps their documents in their bag. This box is for the kitchen and these boxes are for our books. My friend is coming to help us.
rubric: Choose possessives from the noun and owner.
Use son/sa/ses for each generic individual.
Distinguish cette from cet and ces.
